subject: Hosted API volume pricing for Acme Labs (12B/mo)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmelabs.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-29T16:12:00Z
Subject: Interest in hosted API pricing for ~12B tokens/month

Hi Jonas —

We're evaluating Redwood for our inference backend. Rough profile attached (acme_volume_profile.xlsx) but high level: ~12B tokens/month steady-state (mix of short and medium sequences), occasional daily bursts up to 700M tokens. Key asks: baseline hosted API rates, multi-month commit discounts, overage handling, and any accelerator credits you can provide for an early-stage integration.

Can you share a baseline rate card and an example blended price for a 12-month, 10–12B commitment? Also include SLA/latency targets for hosted endpoints and any data residency notes. Procurement will be looped in after we see numbers.

Thanks —
Liam O'Connor
Head of ML Platforms
Acme Labs
liam@acmelabs.com

Attachment: acme_volume_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet, 42KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmelabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-30T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Interest in hosted API pricing for ~12B tokens/month

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the profile. Quick summary below (attached full rate card). Happy to do a 30–45 minute call to walk through scenarios.

Proposed Hosted API baseline (list price per 1k tokens):
- 0–500M: $0.0045 / 1k tokens
- 500M–2B: $0.0038 / 1k tokens
- 2B–10B: $0.0032 / 1k tokens
- 10B+: custom enterprise pricing (typically an additional 10–25% step-down depending on term & commitment)

Example committed proposal (12-month, 10B committed):
- Committed blended: $0.0029 / 1k tokens (≈19% discount vs list at scale)
- First 3 months: accelerator credit equal to $100k in token value to cover initial testing/bursting
- Overage: billed at committed blended rate for the first 10% overage, then list tier rates beyond that (we can also cap monthly overage for the first quarter).

SLA: 99.9% uptime for hosted API endpoints with SLO-based latency targets (p50 < 50ms on small-context requests; p95 targets depend on model family). We can include more specific latency SLOs for pinned model variants in the MSA.

Next steps: if these high-level numbers look reasonable I can ask our finance team to generate a deal worksheet (deal id HUBSPOT-9876) and share a DocuSign for a 12-month commitment.

Attached: redwood_hosted_ratecard_v3.pdf

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-02T14:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Interest in hosted API pricing for ~12B tokens/month (internal notes)

Jonas — quick internal notes before we push final terms to Acme: 
- Margin check: 12B committed at $0.0029/k still gives ~35% gross margin at standard model mix (assuming quantized runtime). Confirmed with infra.
- Flex: propose phased commit: 6 months at 6B, 6 months at 12B (we advertise blended as if 10B to make offer more compelling). This reduces initial capacity commitment risk.
- Accelerator: $100k credit is fine; alternatively offer 50% discount for first month + $50k credit to preserve billable runway.
- Legal ask: include a 30-day termination right for material SLA breaches; procurement will push back on auto-renew.
- I'll own finance signoff and sequencing. We should lock the deal in HubSpot (HUBSPOT-9876) and generate a PSA/Rate Addendum template.

cc: marissa for deal orchestration with Acme.

Ben
Head of Sales Ops

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmelabs.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, procurement@acmelabs.com
Date: 2026-07-10T11:08:00Z
Subject: Proposal: phased commitment + accelerator credits (Acme Labs)

Hi Liam — following up with a concrete proposal based on your profile and our internal guidance. Attaching the ratecard again and a short summary here so procurement has something to review quickly.

Summary commercial proposal
- Term: 12 months (phased commit)
  - Months 1–6: committed 6B tokens/month
  - Months 7–12: committed 12B tokens/month
- Pricing (committed blended): $0.00295 / 1k tokens (this is the blended billing rate across the 12 months)
- Accelerator: $100k in credits applied in month 1–3 (applies as monthly credit, not rollover)
- Overage: first 10% per month billed at committed blended; >10% billed at list tier rates; we can negotiate a monthly overage cap for the first quarter.
- Onboarding credit: one-time implementation credit (up to $25k) if we provide a joint onboarding plan and milestones.

Procurement and legal notes:
- We will provide a standard MSA + Rate Addendum; DocuSign link included below. Please review the termination and SLA section; our legal can be flexible on auto-renew language with a 60-day notice.

DocuSign (MSA + Rate Addendum): https://www.docusign.com/IN-PROD/link-to-acme-msasample
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/9876

If you confirm, I can issue the DocuSign and we will queue finance to finalize the billing schedule. Can we schedule a 30-min call early next week to finalize commercial terms?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_hosted_ratecard_v3.pdf (redwood hosted pricing, 12 pages)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmelabs.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmelabs.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-14T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased commitment + accelerator credits (Acme Labs)

Thanks Marissa — this looks reasonable and aligns with our internal forecast. A few clarifying items before we sign: 

1) Overage calc: please provide a simple monthly example invoice for a month where we hit 7B (month 4) and for a month where we hit 13B (month 9) showing line-items (committed discount, overage at blended, overage at list).
2) Credits: please confirm the $100k accelerator will be consumed as monthly credits across months 1–3 (we prefer monthly distribution rather than a single upfront). Your note says "applies as monthly credit" but want explicit amortization on the Docusign schedule.
3) SOC 2 / security evidence: procurement will need SOC 2 Type II and network diagrams. We'd like a link or a one-page evidence bundle prior to agreement execution.

If you can update the DocuSign with the amortization schedule and drop the SOC 2 bundle link in the DocuSign Q&A, procurement will move quickly.

I'll stand by for the invoice examples and the updated DocuSign.

-Liam

Acme Labs Procurement CC'd: procurement@acmelabs.com
